meta.title: MNT Reform 2 · dead 3.3 V rail
meta.author: DEADBOARD
meta.description: An open-hardware laptop mainboard (529 parts) that came back from a repair desk: it powers up, but the system never starts. The bench supply is clipped onto the gated input rail. Find out why the 3.3 V rail is missing, fix it, and leave the board clean. Bench supply: 30 V on 30V_GATE (rail name 30V_GATE).
hints: Power it up with Solver: SPICE + PWR. Compare the supply current with what a board at idle should draw, then measure +5V, +3V3 and +1V2.
A rail sitting far below its target while its regulator is enabled usually means it is being pulled down. Thermal view, freeze spray or the rosin tool will show you the hot part.
There is also something crusty next to a 5 V capacitor. Isopropyl takes a few scrubs.
meta.credits: MNT Reform 2 motherboard rev 3.0, designed by MNT Research GmbH. Converted and modified (planted faults) for DEADBOARD.
